faq.q: Where does a cactus store water?
faq.a: In its thick, fleshy stem, full of spongy tissue that holds water. A big saguaro can soak up hundreds of litres after a single storm.
asks: How much water can a cactus hold?

faq.a: Spines are leaves that have become thin and hard. They lose far less water than flat leaves, protect the cactus from animals, and their shade and trapped air help keep the stem cooler.

faq.q: Why do cacti open their pores at night?
faq.a: Many cacti use a trick called CAM. They open their stomata in the cool night to take in carbon dioxide and store it, then close them in the hot day and use it for photosynthesis, losing far less water.
asks: How do cacti make food without losing water?

faq.a: Because the stem does the leaves' job. It is full of chlorophyll and makes the cactus's food from sunlight.

faq.q: Can you drink water from a cactus?
faq.a: Usually not safely. The liquid in most cacti is thick and bitter and can make you sick, so survival experts warn against relying on it.

facts: Many cacti use CAM photosynthesis, opening their stomata at night to save water.
Saguaro cacti can grow over 12 metres tall and live for more than 150 years.

quiz.why: Spines are leaves reduced to thin, hard points, which lose very little water.

wrong.1: Roots are underground; spines grow from the stem.
wrong.2: Cacti have separate flowers; spines are leaves.

quiz.say: When do many cacti open their stomata?
quiz.show: When do many cacti open their stomata?
quiz.why: Opening in the cool night lets them take in carbon dioxide while losing much less water.

wrong.1: Opening in the midday heat would waste lots of water.
wrong.2: They take in carbon dioxide every night, not only on rare rainy days.
